reviewed_by: Codex review of release gates after user removed Kali cold build from CI and release testing
reason: The release gate previously spent about 50 minutes building Kali and failed on hosted temporary-layer disk. The user explicitly removed that cold build from CI and release testing. The cold-build case is now manual opt-in outside CI; the real-Core catalog retains both 47- and 46-case shards for the remaining Core journeys without Podman setup. Release sandbox integration keeps its separate small operator-runtime image and no longer pulls Kali. The source change also moves optional conversation naming storage off Core event loop and fixes MCP import error-chip contrast. Validate catalog routing, responsive conversation switching, the production real-Core journeys, and the accessibility audit. Hosted traces showed the conversation state route completed in 33-39 ms on two retries while the hosted LAN request took about 1.2 seconds; a third retry used 1.38 seconds in Core. The browser test now records and bounds Core application time separately from end-to-end delivery, and still exercises the visible A-B-A switch, held history refresh, retry, and reload. The current-main Notes autosave update changed the visible failure action to Retry save; the selected production note recovery case now waits for autosave failure and clicks that action. Local production real-Core replay passed 1/1.
exclusions: The Kali cold-build case is listed but skipped in CI and release runs by explicit user direction; it remains available only as a manual local acceptance test. No native or frontend unit code changed, so those layers are excluded. Python sandbox image tests, unrelated browser journeys, and full suites are excluded. The lightweight release sandbox integration job remains; it does not build Kali.
